---
title: "Executive summary"
---

This report translates the Ridgway's Rail section of the Sound Ecology Pilot
Studies repository into a decision aid for managers. It describes what passive
acoustic monitoring (PAM) can contribute to future studies, what the pilot
demonstrated, and which design decisions should be resolved before committing
to a larger survey.

## Decisions this report supports

Managers can use this report to:

1. Decide whether PAM is appropriate for a monitoring objective;
2. select a recording and analysis design that matches that objective;
3. Distinguish pilot evidence from results that require validation; and
4. Plan a defensible, reproducible field study.

The pilot is best treated as a methods study and serves to inform future studies. Detection probability, call classification, habitat effects, and
availability of independent detections all require validation as there are known discrepancies. 

## How to use the report

The chapters provide a concise management narrative. An html (web) version of this report as well as a downloadable pdf, data products, code, and figures are available in the public github repository. Raw audio and raw detection data may be available upon request.

For a printable copy, select **Download PDF** in the book navigation or use
the PDF link in the top-right menu.
